what_it_does.name: webapp-testing
what_it_does.summary: Instructions, one helper script and three example scripts for testing local web applications with native Python Playwright scripts. The helper with_server.py starts one or more servers, waits until their ports answer, runs an automation command and then stops the servers. The automation navigates to the app, waits for networkidle, takes screenshots or inspects the rendered DOM to find selectors, and then acts with those selectors, with examples for element discovery, static HTML through file:// URLs and console log capture. Use it to verify frontend functionality, debug UI behavior, capture browser screenshots and view browser logs.
tasks: start one or more local servers, run an automation command, then stop them
inspect the rendered DOM and take screenshots to find selectors
click, fill and submit forms with Playwright
automate static HTML files through file:// URLs
what_it_does.author_description: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in a tested page reach the agent, since DOM content and console logs are read into its context without delimiters or sanitisation.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: none in the files, C2 notes that no boundary markers or filtering are used

risks.risk: A --server command built from untrusted input runs arbitrary code with the agent's privileges, since with_server.py passes it to the shell with shell=True.
risks.severity: LOW by C3, SAFE overall by C2

risks.risk: Running the automation against an app connected to real data can change that data, since the examples click buttons and submit forms without asking.
Screenshots and logs written to /tmp and /mnt/user-data/outputs can hold data shown by the app and stay there after the run.

limitations: The bundled scripts can be very large, and reading their source fills the context window, so they are run as black boxes with --help first.
with_server.py checks readiness only by polling the given port on localhost, 30 seconds per server by default.
Inspecting the DOM of a dynamic app before networkidle gives an incomplete picture of the page.
